critique: The limited icy-blue, navy, white, yellow, and coral palette is cohesive, and hard pixel-like edges consistently support the retro presentation. However, the central modal uses several nested borders and mismatched offset shadows, making it heavier and less crisp than the HUD frame. Pixel scale is inconsistent: the skier, trees, flags, snow particles, logo icon, and type operate at unrelated resolutions, with anti-aliased text sitting beside chunky geometry. The slope's dashed tracks and mountain edges vary in thickness, and the tiny face tile near the bottom has no clear construction relationship to other HUD elements. Some white snow details are nearly invisible against the field.
suggestion: Choose a base pixel unit and snap all scene geometry, borders, shadows, icons, and decorative marks to multiples of it. Reduce the central modal to one frame plus one consistent hard offset shadow that matches the top HUD; standardize line thickness across tracks, flags, and mountains. Render or simulate pixel type consistently across title, instructions, and counters, avoiding mixed smooth serif/sans details. Rebuild the skier, trees, HUD shoe, and face marker with a shared sprite resolution and palette, and adjust snow-particle tones so every detail has intentional contrast.
audit_note: Direct independent visual critique from the r0 screenshot and brief only; no generation notes, HTML, other critics, revisions, or scores were inspected.
